source.title: Imbalance Trouble: Revisiting Neural-Collapse Geometry
source.authors: Christos Thrampoulidis; Ganesh Ramachandra Kini; V. Vakilian; Tina Behnia

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present; no truncation or garbling apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-error outcomes for SGD-trained deep networks on CIFAR-10, using the same training-error measure as V1 in a class-imbalanced setting.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results about neural-collapse geometry; those are outside the listed claim versions. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly reports near-zero training classification error for SGD-trained convolutional networks on CIFAR-10, extending V1 to STEP class imbalance. Its main geometric results concern a different question.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct: most deep models reach the near-zero training-error criterion around epoch 120 and continue training to epoch 350. The principal conclusion proposes SELI as an imbalance-invariant geometric characterization, supported by UFM theory and experiments. Asymptotic convergence of GD and deep-network geometries remains conjectural, and observed geometric convergence worsens with imbalance.
record.recipe_differences: Deep-network experiments use cross-entropy with SGD on class-imbalanced datasets; the paper studies geometry and does not specify random initialization.
record.method_sensitivity: For CIFAR10, the first zero-error epoch varies with architecture and imbalance ratio; VGG at R=100 reaches it at epoch 176, compared with ResNet at epoch 120.

fits_no_version.finding: Learned classifier, embedding, and logit geometries approach SELI more closely than ETF under imbalance; geometric convergence slows with increasing imbalance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class imbalance changes neural-collapse geometry and its convergence rate beyond near-zero training error.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical and synthetic UFM results characterize global minimizers and regularization-dependent geometry for a two-layer linear model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: UFM solutions have SELI geometry in the vanishing-regularization limit; convergence of unregularized GD to the relevant global minimizers remains conjectural.

record.problems: Initialization and model sizes are not stated. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the zero-error epochs. The zero-error criterion permits 0.2% error for majority classes.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, early-stopping effects, and comparisons across regularization recipes. Random initialization is not documented in the supplied text.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local-minimum frequencies and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and controlled comparisons of plain networks with identity shortcuts.
Initialization comparisons, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, recovery, and divergence.
Controlled batch-normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: All eight epoch values match Table 2. The stated zero-error criterion permits 0.2% error for majority classes and specifies 0.00% for minority classes with n_min <= 500. This supports near-zero classification error, without establishing exactly zero error or near-zero cross-entropy loss. No uncertainty estimates or initialization details are supplied.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and other regularized recipes are not tested. Random initialization and model sizes are not stated.
